name: s4098 Transit incident operations reference (ground truth for the Evaluator Agent)
source: Field rules from my HW4 incident schema (categories, required fields, codes, route codes in s4098_rel) plus the operating rules of the fictional s4098 Transit agency used in this course project.

facts.title: Allowed incident categories
facts.fact: An incident category must be exactly one of four values: delay, collision, service-suspension, infrastructure-issue.

facts.title: Required fields of a new incident report
facts.fact: A new incident report must include six required fields: incidentTitle, routeLine, submitterEmail, description, category and termsAccepted.

facts.title: Incident code format
facts.fact: Incident codes use the format INC- followed by six digits, for example INC-000042.

facts.title: When lateness becomes a delay incident
facts.fact: A late vehicle is logged as a delay incident when it is 10 or more minutes behind schedule.

facts.title: Delay escalation to Severity 2
facts.fact: A delay of 30 minutes or more is escalated to Severity 2 and the duty supervisor is paged.

facts.title: Severity 1 criteria
facts.fact: Severity 1 applies to any incident with an injury or with more than 200 passengers affected.

facts.title: When to request a bus bridge
facts.fact: A bus bridge (replacement buses) is requested when a light-rail service suspension is expected to last more than 20 minutes.

facts.title: Rider alert deadline
facts.fact: A rider alert must be posted on the app and station displays within 10 minutes of confirming a service suspension.

facts.title: Operator steps after a collision
facts.fact: After a collision the operator stops the vehicle and calls the Operations Control Center (OCC); the vehicle stays out of service until a supervisor inspects it.

facts.title: Maintenance ticket deadline for infrastructure issues
facts.fact: An infrastructure-issue incident needs a maintenance ticket opened within 4 hours of the report.

facts.title: Follow-up note before closing
facts.fact: Every incident needs a follow_up note within 48 hours; only then can it be closed.

facts.title: Reporting long suspensions to the city
facts.fact: A service suspension longer than 60 minutes must be reported to the San Jose Department of Transportation.

facts.title: Types of related notes
facts.fact: A related note attached to an incident has one of three types: operator_note, maintenance_note, follow_up.

facts.title: passengersAffected value
facts.fact: passengersAffected must be a whole number of 0 or more; when the number of affected passengers is unknown, use 0.

facts.title: Extreme heat speed restriction
facts.fact: When the rail temperature is above 120 degrees F, light-rail trains run at no more than 35 mph.

facts.title: Record retention
facts.fact: Incident records are kept for 7 years.

facts.title: Route code of the VTA Orange Line
facts.fact: The VTA Orange Line has route code RT-002 (RT-001 VTA Green Line, RT-003 VTA Route 22, RT-004 VTA Route 522, RT-005 VTA Route 55).

facts.title: termsAccepted must be true
facts.fact: termsAccepted must be true; a report submitted with termsAccepted set to false is rejected with a validation error.

facts.title: submitterEmail validation
facts.fact: submitterEmail must be a valid email address; a report with an invalid email is rejected with a validation error.

out_of_scope_rule: A question that no fact above covers is outside the transit incident reference. The correct behaviour is to say so and not answer it from general knowledge.
